rules.reason: On sm120, vLLM runs DeepSeek-V4.1 through its FlashInfer SM120 backend, which declares 128-token KV blocks (the indexer also uses 128 outside Hopper), while the sliding-window cache uses 32-token pages. The SM120 sparse MLA kernels of FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, the version pinned by vLLM 0.31, are instantiated for 64-token pages only, for both decode and prefill. No block size works for every layer, so the server stops during warmup. This applies to every sm120 GPU (RTX 5080/5090, RTX PRO 6000), on Linux as well.
rules.fixedIn: Not fixed in any release (vLLM 0.31.0 is the latest as of 2026-10-15). It needs vllm-project/vllm#57292 (64-token blocks, still open) together with FlashInfer from main (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5197, included in FlashInfer 0.7.1) and DeepGEMM with vllm-project/DeepGEMM#14; with these three pieces a user started it on 8× RTX PRO 6000 (issue #59203). The alternative PR #56509 starts but produces wrong output.

rules.reason: Without MLA and outside SM10x, FLASH_ATTN is first in priority; on these architectures it resolves to FlashAttention 2 (FA3 only on 9.x, FA4 only on 9.x/10.x/11.x), which accepts head_dim up to 256.

rules.reason: On Hopper, FLASH_ATTN is the first backend and uses FlashAttention 3 by default.
On SM10x (10.0 and 10.3 are the same), the first causal backend is FLASHINFER (TRTLLM-Gen kernels), with FLASH_ATTN (FA4) as the fallback.

FA4 does not exist on these architectures, so for Gemma 4 (mixed head_dim 256/512) vLLM forces TRITON_ATTN on all layers: it starts, but attention runs on the Triton kernel, which is slower than FlashAttention. The Triton kernel with head_dim 512 needs 96 KiB of shared memory (fails on SM75, fits within the ~99 KiB limit of SM86/89/120).

sources.note: vLLM 0.26.0, Quadro RTX 6000 SM75: Triton head_dim 512 requires 98304 B of shared memory (limit 65536); confirms that head_dim 512 goes through the Triton fallback

rules.reason: On Hopper, Gemma 4 sets FlashAttention 4 for all layers (FA3 does not go beyond head_dim 256); with fp8 KV it uses FA3/FA4 per layer.

On SM10x, FLASHINFER (TRTLLM-Gen, head_dim 512 supported) is kept. The MTP crash caused by a missing head_dim 512 cubin was in FlashInfer 0.6.13 and is fixed in 0.6.14; vLLM 0.31 uses FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1.

rules.reason: FlashAttention 3 supports sinks on Hopper (flash_attn_supports_sinks is true for FA3/FA4).
FLASHINFER with TRTLLM-Gen serves sinks if the cubins are available (preinstalled or downloadable from the NVIDIA artifactory); otherwise it switches to FLASH_ATTN with FA4, which supports them.
FA2 does not support sinks; FLASHINFER serves them with XQA decode and BatchAttentionWithAttentionSinkWrapper prefill if the XQA cubins are available, otherwise it falls back to TRITON_ATTN (slower).

On SM10x the default backend is FLASHINFER, and with Llama 4 chunked local attention a prefill longer than attention_chunk_size with a small max_num_seqs raises ValueError 'provided out is the wrong size'; fix not merged.

rules.reason: ChunkedLocalAttention wraps the architecture's default backend with virtual batches, so it adds no architecture constraints; however, these layers are not captured in CUDA graphs (AttentionCGSupport.NEVER).
FLASH_ATTN_MLA (9.x only), FLASHMLA (9.x/10.x) and FLASHINFER_MLA (10.x) are discarded, so TRITON_MLA is used for decode; MLA prefill uses FlashAttention 2.
On Hopper, the first MLA backend is FLASH_ATTN_MLA (FA3), with dense FLASHMLA as the second choice.
On SM10x (10.0 and 10.3), the first MLA backend is FLASHINFER_MLA (block size 32/64, qk_nope_head_dim must be 64/128/192), then CUTLASS_MLA.
On SM12x the only dense MLA backend in the list is TRITON_MLA (no FlashMLA, CUTLASS MLA or FlashInfer MLA), which accepts any architecture.

FA2 does not support fp8 KV, so vLLM selects another attention backend (FLASHINFER for most models, with Q in bf16). There are open bugs on this path: with pip and no nvcc, FlashInfer is selected but does not compile (crash 'Could not find nvcc'), and with checkpoints that have q_scale the output is wrong.
